findings.reason: the author must state section_of's behaviour for an input with no second segment (return the path unchanged, or refuse) and make validation.py's replacement preserve the existing fallback, which is a contract decision the section currently leaves open.
findings.text: section_of is specified as `<ids>/<first segment>` but one of the three copies it must replace, imas_codex/ids/validation.py:842 (`section = "/".join(parts[:2]) if len(parts) >= 2 else ids_name`), has an explicit fallback for a path with fewer than two segments that the specified contract does not carry; §8 says validation.py "calls it in place of its re-derivation", so unless section_of defines the single- or zero-segment case, the replacement silently changes behaviour on a bare-IDS target_id and the map stage's section-level guard can compare against an undefined section

findings.reason: the section's own interface-budget paragraph would be rewritten to describe the change the two unlanded nodes actually make, rather than a revision that has already shipped.
findings.text: the section's public-definition accounting ("count_sources_by_mapping_status and the workers.py copy of count_candidates_by_route are deleted") presents two deletions as part of §8's surface budget, but both are already absent at HEAD: grep shows count_candidates_by_route defined only at imas_codex/ids/graph_ops.py:796 and no count_sources_by_mapping_status anywhere, so the two remaining §8 nodes (map-run-chooses-candidates, map-run-maps-each-home) add section_of with no live public-definition retirement to offset it; the section should reconcile the accounting at its head and state, for the remaining nodes, what they retire or why nothing can be

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — section_of(path) is a deep one-function module (small interface, the IDS-top-level-ancestor rule hidden behind it), but its contract is specified only as `<ids>/<first segment>` and does not define the path that has no second segment, which is a case its named replacement site already handles.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the census is complete. Re-ran the plan's own census at HEAD: the MAPS_TO_IMAS create is one site (imas_codex/ids/graph_ops.py:728 MERGE inside write_mapping_binding) and the delete is one site (imas_codex/ids/graph_ops.py:783 inside clear_mapping_bindings); MAPPING_CANDIDATE create is one site (graph_ops.py:537) and delete two (graph_ops.py:530, :838). The section-of rule has exactly the three copies §8 names and no fourth in imas_codex/ (grep for the two-segment derivation returns only graph_ops.py:608, validation.py:842 and the assembler.py:187 prefix test).
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0. §8 names what it retires or merges for each family it touches: it retires mapping_target_path/ids/type and two CLI options, deletes two public definitions, and merges three copies of the section rule into section_of; the strict selection flag reuses the existing CandidateWriteError family (imas_codex/ids/graph_ops.py:25) rather than adding one. The accounting is written against a pre-landing revision, however — see the finding below.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §8 cites and extends the machinery it installs beside (claim_batch in imas_codex/discovery/base/claims.py:255, write_candidates/read_candidates in imas_codex/ids/graph_ops.py, and the three section-rule call sites); no new subsystem is proposed. The one derivation that could have hidden a rebuild — the section-node → TargetType rule — was searched for prior art: imas_codex/core/node_classifier.py:400 (classify_node_pass1) and imas_codex/graph/dd_search.py:409 (_STRUCTURE_TYPES) exist but answer a different question (physics category: quantity/geometry/structural), so extending them is not the honest change.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — select_candidates is a genuinely separate operation, not a thin wrapper: §8 justifies it in its own text (write_candidates deletes and rewrites every edge of a source, while a pick must flag existing edges without disturbing the shortlist), and read_candidates collapses each source's edges, section and section attributes into one query behind one signature.
